summary.text: Wave-particle duality is the idea that light and electrons can act like waves or like particles, depending on how you set up the experiment.
Neither the classical picture of a wave nor that of a particle fully describes a quantum object, and the word duality was coined to name that clash.
Light showed wave behavior first and particle behavior later, while electrons went the opposite way, so each needed both pictures.

facts.label: Newton versus Huygens
facts.value: Newton favored light as particles; Huygens argued for waves

facts.label: Young's experiments
facts.value: Interference experiments in 1801 supported the wave model of light

facts.label: Electron waves confirmed
facts.value: Two separate experiments confirmed electron waves in 1927

facts.label: Beyond electrons
facts.value: Helium atoms and hydrogen molecules also showed wave behavior

facts.label: Compton's role
facts.value: Compton's 1922-1924 experiments showed light carries momentum

items.prompt: A friend says, 'An electron is a tiny ball, and any wave-like result must be a measurement error.' What does the history of duality suggest?

options.label: Electrons really are tiny balls, and the wave results are errors
Electrons act as particles in some tests and waves in others
Electrons are waves only and never show particle behavior
Electrons switch roles randomly regardless of the experiment

items.explain: Early experiments showed electrons behaving like particles, and later ones showed wave-like behavior. Which one appears depends on the experimental circumstances.

items.prompt: Why did physicists coin a special name, duality, for light and electrons?

options.label: The wave and particle pictures each failed to describe them fully
Light and electrons were found to be made of the same material
Experiments proved the wave picture was wrong for both of them
Scientists wanted a single word for all of quantum theory

items.explain: The name arose to label seeming contradictions: classical wave or particle concepts could not fully describe quantum objects.

items.prompt: In 1801 a researcher sends light through two narrow openings and sees bands of bright and dark. Which view of light does this support?

options.label: Light is a stream of tiny bullets that bounce off the edges
Light is both a wave and a particle at exactly the same moment
Light behaves as a wave, which is what interference shows
Light is made of electrons traveling in straight lines

items.explain: Young's interference experiments validated Huygens' wave model of light.

items.prompt: A physicist finds a hot cavity can only change its energy in small fixed steps tied to frequency. Which kind of behavior did Planck's and Einstein's work point to?

options.label: Smooth continuous waves
Random noise with no pattern
Standing waves around a nucleus
Discrete, particle-like packets of energy

items.explain: Planck's minimal energy increment and Einstein's discrete photon energies both indicated particle behavior in light.

items.prompt: In 1927 electrons fired at thin nickel film produced rings on a detector. What did this confirm about electrons?

options.label: They carry a larger charge than first thought
They are heavier than atoms of nickel itself
They can show wave behavior, since diffraction is a wave effect
They are never able to behave like particles

items.explain: The concentric diffraction rings observed by Thomson and Reid confirmed the wave nature of electrons.

items.prompt: Stern sent helium atoms at crystals in the 1930s and saw wave behavior. What did this add to the picture?

options.label: Wave behavior is a general property of matter, not just electrons
Only light and electrons can ever act as waves
Atoms are always lighter than the electrons
Crystals are what create waves in any particle

items.explain: Crystal diffraction with helium atoms and hydrogen molecules showed wave behavior is not limited to electrons.
